I was very disappointed in the work done on my car by Tin Lizzie.  They installed custom carpet in my 1972 Alfa Romeo GTV, and it ended up costing me a fair amount of money and frustration to fix things they broke.  The worst issue was they screwed a large screw completely through the wiring harness that runs to the rear of the vehicle -- I don't know if they could have hit it more dead center if they tried.  At that point, they should have realized something was wrong because the car no longer ran because the electric fuel pump wire was in that harness.  Even worse, they didn't bother to tell me that the car wasn't running until several weeks later when I arrived to pick the car up!  It's a good thing I had a trailer and didn't plan to drive it home!  I ended up taking the car to an Italian car specialist to diagnose and fix the electrical problems caused by the short circuit and damaged wire, and that really put me behind the 8 ball as I'm trying to get this car finished.  Also, the car was promised to be done three times; the first two times it wasn't ready.  Usually that's not a big deal, but I'm active duty Army and live out of state (and they know this), so I burned up leave unnecessarily because the car wasn't ready when they said it would be, and I had already taken leave.  They also had trouble with seemingly simple tasks, like removing seats and removing a bolt-in rollcage.  The communication was also very limited; in the several months that they had the car, I think they may have called once with an update or a question.  Otherwise, I had to call them every week to find out what was happening.  Sorry for writing a book, but I waited for a few months after getting the car back to write this review and I've calmed down considerably.  I also generally don't leave negative reviews, but I just didn't feel right not giving potential customers some feedback on my experience.  In closing, I will say that Lucinda and Joel are both kind and cordial, their prices are reasonable, and I wish them the best of luck moving forward.  However, I also hope they learned from the mistakes made on my car.  Scott Walters
